title: Alphabet
welcome_text: Deaf people live around the world. British Sign Language (BSL) is one of many sign languages. Australian Sign Language (Auslan) has historical links with BSL; American Sign Language (ASL) developed separately and is quite different.
scenario_prompt: How many sign languages can you name? Why might sign languages differ between countries?

title: Alphabet and Greetings
welcome_text: Learning greetings is a first step towards meeting people through BSL. Deaf identity and language mean different things to different people.
scenario_prompt: Why might learning someone’s language matter beyond simply finding a way to communicate?

title: Numbers and Everyday Living
welcome_text: Everyday words and numbers can vary across BSL communities. Communication access matters at work, school and in daily life.
scenario_prompt: What would help you participate fully in a workplace where communication was not accessible to you?

title: Weather and Feelings
welcome_text: In BSL, facial expression, head movement and mouth patterns all contribute to grammar and meaninsg, as well as emotion.
scenario_prompt: How might a message change if you could see someone’s hands but not their face?

title: Days and Months
welcome_text: Deaf history includes times when sign languages were discouraged in education, as well as milestones in community life and sport.
scenario_prompt: Why is Deaf history relevant when studying BSL today?

title: Sentence Structure and Gesturing
welcome_text: BSL is a visual-spatial language. Signers use space, movement and facial grammar to show relationships and tell stories.
scenario_prompt: How could you show the location and movement of two cars using the space in front of you?

title: Pets, Colours and Placement
welcome_text: Deaf people use many ways to access information at home, including hearing dogs, visual alerts and vibration alerts.
scenario_prompt: If you could not hear a doorbell or alarm, what changes could help at home?

title: Transport and Directions
welcome_text: Audio-only announcements can make travel difficult for Deaf passengers. Visual information and clear communication support independence.
scenario_prompt: A platform change is announced only over a loudspeaker. What could the station do?

title: Family
welcome_text: Most deaf children are born to hearing parents. Families may be new to deafness and sign language; early access to language is important.
scenario_prompt: What might a family want to learn after discovering their child is deaf?

title: Descriptions and Clothes
welcome_text: Sign names are part of Deaf cultural practice. Naming conventions vary, and sign names are often given within community relationships.
scenario_prompt: Why learn Deaf cultural conventions before using or creating a sign name?

title: Recap
welcome_text: Deaf clubs and community networks have provided places to meet, share language and culture, build friendships and organise for change.
scenario_prompt: What might Deaf people gain from meeting others who share their language and experiences?

title: Food and Drink
welcome_text: Restaurants can create communication barriers. Lipreading is difficult: many speech sounds look alike on the lips, and context cannot fill every gap.
scenario_prompt: Imagine ordering in a busy café while the server looks away. What could they do to help?

title: Home and Hobbies
welcome_text: Deaf people have varied relationships with music and sound, including through hearing, vibration, signed performance, dance and visual elements.
scenario_prompt: What different ways could someone experience rhythm or music?

title: People, Animals and Objects
welcome_text: BSL uses depicting and classifier constructions to show an object’s shape, position or movement in signing space.
scenario_prompt: How could you describe a room’s layout using the space around you?

title: Final Presentations and Conversations
welcome_text: Visual attention and turn-taking cues help signed conversations flow. Respectful communication includes checking preferences and asking for clarification.
scenario_prompt: What would you do if you did not understand a sign during a conversation?
